BACKUP HEALTH AND RESTORE DRILL
No drill recorded

Select a previously saved backup, using the decryption controls above. The complete bundle is checked, then a limited sample is actually restored and read back in temporary PostgreSQL tables. The transaction is rolled back; your live files and settings are not replaced. The decrypted bundle goes to this Fusion server; PostgreSQL temporary tables and indexes may put plaintext on its disk, and rollback is not secure erasure. This does not test Private-volume unlocking, other devices or the continued health of the saved copy.

Choose backup to drill…
Clear local drill status
The reminder is shown only when this Backup window is open; it is not an automatic monthly job or notification. Status is kept on this browser without file names, contents or secrets. A pass describes only the selected copy and sampled restore at that time, not all backups.
SCOPE AND KEY CUSTODY
Config bundles contain editable settings only. Data bundles contain current, non-trashed Fusion files, folders and notes; they do not include tasks, contacts, file history, trash, or every app database. This is not an incremental timeline or an automatic scheduled restore drill. Plain backups are readable and their SHA-256 checksum detects corruption but does not authenticate the source. Encrypted downloads use PBKDF2-SHA256 (600,000 iterations) and authenticated AES-GCM. The passphrase and optional recovery key stay in this browser; decrypted contents are sent to this Fusion server when restoring. Passphrase-only downloads have no separate recovery key. There is no escrow; for a recovery-key download either secret can decrypt it, and losing both makes it unreadable.

History covers copies made inside Fusion plus explicit captures. Copies made in other apps are invisible until you press “Capture”: browsers only allow clipboard reads with focus and a user gesture, and there is no IME route for a web app. History lives in memory and is gone on reload — by design, since clipboards carry secrets. SCOPE AND KEY CUSTODY
Config bundles contain editable settings only. Data bundles contain current, non-trashed Fusion files, folders and notes; they do not include tasks, contacts, file history, trash, or every app database. This is not an incremental timeline or an automatic scheduled restore drill. Plain backups are readable and their SHA-256 checksum detects corruption but does not authenticate the source. Encrypted downloads use PBKDF2-SHA256 (600,000 iterations) and authenticated AES-GCM. The passphrase and optional recovery key stay in this browser; decrypted contents are sent to this Fusion server when restoring. Passphrase-only downloads have no separate recovery key. There is no escrow; for a recovery-key download either secret can decrypt it, and losing both makes it unreadable.

History covers copies made inside Fusion plus explicit captures. Copies made in other apps are invisible until you press “Capture”: browsers only allow clipboard reads with focus and a user gesture, and there is no IME route for a web app. History lives in memory and is gone on reload — by design, since clipboards carry secrets.
